subject: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-098.turn2.draft.md
summary: Turn 2 resolves the two original MUST-FIX mechanics. From the second release onward, the previous digest-pinned binary and candidate are measured on the same current VMs and weekly images do not suppress the 10% rule. The command-by-binary cold/warm sequence now purges before every cold observation, places each warm observation immediately after its matching cold run, enumerates G04 help/version/doctor steady and peak series, requires every G04 absolute sample to pass, and defines regression aggregates without pooling. One new MUST-FIX remains: the formula computes and enforces p50/p95/p99 for both cold and warm G03 series, thereby adding a warm-p50 10% gate that is not one of D-006's deliberately five governed startup percentiles. The preflight repair also remains partial because label and process architecture are not actually observed and the proposed image fields do not identify the runner image. Reversibility omits restoration of exact-OS and the original D-006 runner classes. Condition 4 therefore cannot yet move from 16 of 18 PARTLY MET to MET.

objections.title: The formula silently adds a warm-p50 regression gate outside D-006
objections.finding: Adopted D-006 governs exactly five startup percentiles: cold p50/p95/p99 and warm p95/p99. D-098 lines 61-65 define p50/p95/p99 for every command in every state, and lines 107-112 require the 1.10 ratio for all three percentiles of every G03 series. That makes warm p50 an operative sixth regression metric even though D-098 says its successor is scoped to exact-machine/exact-OS and that D-006's numeric regime stands. Computing warm p50 for diagnostics would be harmless; using it to fail qualification is a new preference-laden threshold-surface decision that is neither identified nor warranted.
evidence: Adopted COORD D-006 clause 3 lists cold p50, p95, p99 and warm p95, p99 and explicitly records that all five startup percentiles are bounded.
D-098 turn 2 lines 61-65 create three quantiles for both cold and warm series, and lines 107-112 apply the 10% test to each of those three without a state-specific exception.
D-098 lines 33-38 scope the successor to exact-machine/exact-OS and say the D-006 numerals and activation rule stand; no alternative or class-trade row discloses adding warm p50.
objections.impact: A second-or-later release can fail on warm p50 even when every D-006 absolute and regression quantity passes. That silently changes the product gate while claiming only a runner-class successor, so the contract is not yet a faithful D-006 successor and cannot support G03 naming or condition-4 MET.
objections.requiredRepair: Make the operative G03 quantile set state-specific: cold uses p50/p95/p99 and warm uses p95/p99. Warm p50 may be retained as non-operative telemetry if clearly labeled. Apply the paired 10% formula only to those five D-006 quantities. If warm p50 is intentionally a new gate, explicitly widen the preference-laden successor scope, record the new requirement and warrant, and stop saying the D-006 threshold surface is unchanged. Refreeze after repair.

objections.title: The claimed fail-closed observability repair is still incomplete
objections.finding: The subject adds useful commands, but preflight item 1 still says only 'label exact' with no source for the actual workflow label, and item 2 defines host and executable observations while stating 'process arch: same as host' rather than measuring the process architecture. The macOS translation branch then requires independent matching host/process facts even though the process fact remains circular. Image identity is also not captured: `ImageOS` is at most an OS/image family, while `RUNNER_TRACKING_ID` is a runner process-cleanup tracking value, not an image version; the OS-plus-kernel fallback does not uniquely identify a weekly runner image. GitHub's runner-images project directs users to the job's `Set up job` log to identify the image version. Finally, storage sits inside a section titled fail-closed but explicitly never fails, and public-repository context is part of the class without an observation.
evidence: D-098 lines 123-147 contain no label field, no process-architecture probe, and no true runner-image version field.

GitHub's official default-variable reference identifies supported runner facts such as RUNNER_ARCH/RUNNER_OS but does not define RUNNER_TRACKING_ID as image identity: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/variables .
GitHub's runner-images README says the image version used by a build is reported in the `Set up job` log: https://github.com/actions/runner-images .
GitHub's runner repository documents RUNNER_TRACKING_ID in process-cleanup behavior rather than image identification: https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/598 .
objections.impact: An implementation can assert rather than verify process architecture, admit the right resources under the wrong label/repository class, and record a per-job cleanup token as if it identified the weekly image. That leaves independent reproductions unable to audit the paired strata the contract claims to retain.
objections.requiredRepair: Record the pinned `runs-on` literal from the workflow/measurement manifest and verify public-repository context; measure process architecture from the launched binary/process rather than assigning it from host architecture; normalize host/executable/process results per platform; and capture the actual runner image version/release identifier from the supported job metadata or `Set up job` record. Move storage to an explicitly audit-only item or define a genuine fail-closed class observable. Preserve the existing translation rejection semantics.

objections.title: The overturn recipe restores only part of the superseded D-006 contract
objections.finding: D-098 lines 35-47 supersede both exact-machine and exact-OS requirements and replace all four D-006 runner classes, including RAM changes on macOS arm64 and Linux. The reversibility section restores only 'D-006's pre-successor exact-machine requirement.' It does not expressly restore the exact-OS naming obligation or the original M1-class 8 GB, native-Intel, and 4-vCPU/8-GB Linux classes. The file-08 cell/count restoration is otherwise complete.
evidence: D-098 lines 35-38 identify exact-machine and exact-OS as separate superseded obligations.
D-098 lines 42-47 record a replacement class for each platform.
D-098 lines 227-231 mention only the exact-machine requirement after listing file-08 reversions.
objections.impact: C-D098 could leave the governing runner/OS contract ambiguous even after the two identifiers and readiness text are restored to their reserved state.
objections.requiredRepair: State that overturn restores D-006's full pre-successor runner classes and its exact-machine, exact-OS, cache-state, product-sign-off, and native-Intel-procurability naming obligations, in addition to the already listed file-08 reversions. Do not imply that overturn changes D-006's numeric thresholds.
